epigraphs.text: The forms of liberty may remain long after the spirit has vanished.
Every unchecked emergency becomes a precedent, and every precedent a quiet amendment to the constitution.
Power rarely announces that it has changed hands; it simply begins to act as if it never needed permission.

long_synopsis: Week 62 of Trump’s second term registered no net movement on the Democracy Clock, holding at 8:13 p.m., but only because resistance absorbed a surge of strain. Abroad, the Iran war hardened into an executive project: threats to “obliterate” power plants, large new deployments, sanctions maneuvers, and even acknowledgment of an unauthorized “military operation,” all shaped by lobbying from Saudi and Israeli leaders. At home, a prolonged DHS shutdown became leverage for immigration and voting demands, with ICE agents in tactical gear screening passengers and an executive order improvising pay for TSA workers. Parallel efforts sought to narrow and centralize voting through the SAVE America Act, litigation over mail ballots, ballot seizures, and a draft order to end machine and mail voting. Immigration enforcement intensified, courts and states pushed back case by case, and law and security institutions bent further toward partisan loyalty. Meanwhile, money and foreign investment threaded through health, energy, and Middle East policy, and Trump personalized national symbols and memory, even as “No Kings” protests and targeted lawsuits signaled a fragile but real civic countercurrent.
